review_output.summary: When no key can reach a quorum, the loop now breaks at once instead of waiting a grace period, so it stops collecting error responses. A `CommunicationError::Trusted(..)` error that later replies would have produced becomes a `NoConsensus` or `Sample` error.
review_output.failure_scenario: 4 validators of equal weight (quorum 3, validity 2), running `synchronize_received_certificates_from_validators`. Validator A times out with a network error; validator B returns `InactiveChain`. Now remaining=2 and highest=0, so 0+2<3 and the loop breaks. Before, the grace period let validator C's `InactiveChain` arrive, which gave `Trusted(InactiveChain)`, and the caller (client/mod.rs:1526) returned Ok(()). Now it gets `Sample([...])` and passes the error up, so syncing an inactive chain fails. Assertions expecting `Trusted` (e.g. client_tests.rs:405/413) also become more timing-sensitive.

review_output.summary: A change described as "make the grace period configurable" also quietly halves the default from 0.2 to 0.1. Every existing caller passes `None`, so all quorum calls now wait half as long for extra validators.
review_output.failure_scenario: Quorum reached after 1s: extra validators used to get 200ms, now 100ms. Fewer late votes and errors are collected in every `communicate_with_quorum` call (block proposals, `send_chain_update`, syncing). This can shrink the vote sets and error samples returned, with no caller having opted in.

review_output.summary: `Duration::mul_f64(grace_period)` panics if the value is negative, NaN, infinite or overflows. The new public `grace_period: impl Into<Option<f64>>` parameter accepts any f64 with no check.
review_output.failure_scenario: A caller passes `Some(-0.1)` or `Some(f64::NAN)` (e.g. from a future config value). When quorum is reached, `start_time.elapsed().mul_f64(grace_period)` panics and crashes the client task.

review_output.summary: The grace period isn't made configurable in any way a user can reach: all four call sites hard-code `None`, and nothing is threaded through the ChainClient options or config.
review_output.failure_scenario: An operator who wants to tune the grace period can't; the only effect of the change is a new unused parameter plus a changed constant. The fix belongs in the client's options (e.g. a `grace_period` field on ChainClient passed to each call), not in `None` repeated at each call site.

review_output.summary: Trailing whitespace was added on doc line 34 (`contribute `) and comment line 178 (`more values `).
review_output.failure_scenario: CI runs `cargo fmt -- --check` (.github/workflows/rust.yml:296,360). rustfmt strips trailing whitespace, so the format check fails and the PR can't pass CI.

review_output.summary: The new doc comment says other validators get extra time only 'If `grace_period` is specified', but with `None` the code still applies `DEFAULT_GRACE_PERIOD`. It also no longer mentions that the loop stops early when no quorum is possible.
review_output.failure_scenario: A reader thinks passing `None` turns off the grace wait. To actually turn it off they would have to pass `Some(0.0)`, which the doc never mentions, so callers that want no delay get 10% extra latency.

review_output.summary: The loop label `'vote_wait` is not needed: there is only one loop, so a plain `break` does the same thing.
review_output.failure_scenario: Adds a label and a labelled break to a single loop with no nesting; slightly more to read for no benefit.

review_output.summary: The parameter is explained with a plain `//` comment inside the argument list, which repeats the function doc. Rustdoc doesn't render it.
review_output.failure_scenario: The same information lives in two places that can drift apart. Documenting it only in the function doc, or giving it a proper type (e.g. a `GracePeriod` newtype), would be clearer.

review_output.summary: The typo fix corrected "Reponse" but left "ceritifcates" misspelled in the same error message.
review_output.failure_scenario: Users still see "Response doesn't contain requested ceritifcates", and anyone grepping logs for "certificates" misses this error.
